A new look for the desktop app, plus Auto colour grading, a Stats card, an MCP server and older DSLRs over USB.

## New

- The desktop window is redone. Every card has an icon rail, sliders fill to show what they mean, the camera has dials, and things move the same way everywhere (or not at all with the system's reduced motion setting).
- Four looks under Look in Settings: Dark, Classic (the old deep blue), OLED and Light.
- Tooltips with a name, what the control does and a hint. They stay quiet while you adjust something and show quickly while you read.
- Settings is redone in the same style and opens fast.
- **Auto** on the Colour grading card sets Temperature, Tint, Gamma, Gain, Lift, Contrast, Highlights and Saturation from about a second of frames. Faces keep natural skin tones. It fetches the vision pack if it isn't there yet, and the sliders stay yours to change afterwards.
- A **Vibrance** slider in Colour grading.
- **Stats** is an optional card with frames in and out, repeated and dropped frames and why, the link, bitrate, delay, and the phone's heat and encoder. **Nerd** adds each step's time, what each plugin costs and the app's CPU and memory. Every line has a star that pins it to the bottom bar.
- **MCP** is an optional plugin that lets an AI app like Claude Desktop read and change Telescope's settings, with a Read only switch and a button in the top bar that undoes what it changed. `docs/mcp.md` has the details.
- Older DSLRs show up in the device picker on Linux. The Webcam card has focus, aperture, exposure compensation and white balance, and the Photos card takes photos with them, RAW and JPEG together.

## Changed

- "Shape" is **Aspect ratio** and "Things in hand" is **Show hands**.
- Framing levels end at the head, chest, belt and feet, zoom follows the Max zoom setting and the Framing bubble shows a stand-in scene.
- The pan map outlines the phone's longer lenses, and a zoom change on the phone is followed in the frames so the picture doesn't jump.
- KDE Plasma title bars take the app's colours.

## Fixed

- A crashing JPEG decoder only loses that frame. Three in a row reconnect instead of freezing the picture.
- Over UDP the first keyframe request goes out straight away.
- A webcam writer that won't stop can't get a second one started next to it.
- On Windows 11 the virtual camera waits at most 30 ms for an app that's reading it and drops that frame instead of freezing.
- Webcam sizes that can't reach 15 fps are no longer offered.
- A colour cube with the wrong size is ignored instead of breaking the picture.
- The notes on the phone's screen close again.
